title: Bioorthogonal Noncanonical Amino Acid Tagging (BONCAT) Incubation Protocol
author: Jackie Goordial
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.utkewkw

steps.title: Prepare BSC and UV sterilize
steps.instruction: Wipe the interior of the biosafety cabinet and all work surfaces with 70 % ethanol, then turn on the UV light in the hood for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Sterilize mortar assembly with ethanol flame
steps.instruction: Place the mortar base, cylinder, and piston in a dog bowl on the bench, cover them with ethanol, ignite the ethanol with a grill‑lighter, and allow it to burn off while gently moving the items with a blue chisel. Once the bowl is cool enough to handle, transfer it and its contents to the hood, let it cool under UV light, and UV‑sterilize enough weigh‑boats for later use.

steps.title: Assemble mortar components loosely
steps.instruction: Surface‑sterilize your gloves with ethanol, then carefully assemble the base and cylinder, leaving approximately a half‑turn loose. Insert the piston into the cylinder, touching only the textured region at the top.

steps.title: Weigh rock samples for incubation
steps.instruction: Weigh out the required amount of rock (10 g × N + 1) for the incubation; sterilized weigh‑boats are not needed for this step.

steps.title: Ethanol‑sterilize rocks and transfer to mortar
steps.instruction: Place the weighed rocks in the dog bowl, cover them with ethanol, and surface‑sterilize as done for the mortar. After the bowl cools, move it to the hood, flame‑sterilize tweezers, and use the tweezers to transfer the rocks into the mortar (keep the piston inside the hood whenever possible).

steps.title: Crush rocks with mallet in hood
steps.instruction: Remove the mortar with sample from the hood and place it on a rubber mat on the floor while wearing safety glasses and isolation headphones. Use a mallet to crush the rocks, delivering 15–20 hits per round, and rotate the piston periodically without removing it completely from the cylinder. Continue until the rocks are reduced to a sand‑grain size.

steps.title: Collect and re‑crush powder into weigh‑boat
steps.instruction: Return the mortar to the hood, stand the piston on its end, and unscrew the cylinder from the base. Using a flame‑sterilized spatula, chisel the caked powder into a UV‑sterilized weigh‑boat. Remove any large uncrushed pieces with flame‑sterilized tweezers or spatula into another sterile weigh‑boat and re‑crush them to sand‑grain size. (Alternative: transfer the powder directly into a sterile Falcon tube.)

steps.title: Weigh final sample into sterile container
steps.instruction: Cover the weigh‑boat with another weigh‑boat, remove it from the hood, and bring it to the bench near a balance. Weigh the desired amount (usually 10 g) into a UV‑sterilized weigh‑boat using ethanol and a flame‑sterilized spatula, working quickly to avoid contamination. (Alternative: use a sterile Falcon tube as described above.)

steps.title: Set up BONCAT incubation mixture
steps.instruction: In the hood, add the measured rock powder to a 50 ml Falcon tube, add 10 ml of BSM media, and add the chosen BONCAT amino‑acid analog (typically HPG or AHA) to the desired final concentration. Cover the tube with aluminum foil to keep the sample dark.

steps.title: Incubate at desired conditions
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture for the required time period at the desired temperature; conditions depend on the specific experiment and sample.
